演題名: ゲノム編集を用いた遅発性アルツハイマー病リスク関連SHARPINバリアントの機能解析
英語抄録: Despite the large-scale genomic cohort studies that identified many novel genetic variants associated with the risk of late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD), the direct biological relevance of these variants remains unresolved. We have explored LOAD-risk genetic factors in Japanese patients and identified a rare functional SHARPIN variant, rs572750141 (p.Gly186Arg), that is associated with LOAD. Recent large-scale Caucasian GWAS meta-analyses have identified additional common SHARPIN variants associated with LOAD, suggesting SHARPIN's significant role in LOAD pathogenesis. To elucidate the role of SHARPIN variants in disease pathogenesis, we performed functional analyses using knock-in cells and mice generated through genome editing using CRISPR/Cas9. We performed the knock-in of the targeted SNV into cultured cells and obtained SHARPIN G186R homozygous cells by single-cell cloning. Using these knock-in cell lines, we found a suppressed NF-κB pathway and increased amyloid-β secretion into the culture medium. Then, we introduced the Sharpin G183R, which is equivalent to the human SHARPIN G186R, into mice and conducted behavioral analyses that revealed increased persistent behavior and anxiety toward stimuli. Furthermore, we prepared primary microglia from the knock-in mice and performed RNA-Seq analysis. We are now conducting comprehensive analyses of gene expression, pathways, and networks. The differential expression analysis has identified genes with altered expression in knock-in microglia. Further investigation may elucidate the mechanism underlying the onset of LOAD.

演題名: ポリジェニックリスク解析がナルコレプシー1型・2型の共通遺伝基盤を解明（HLA-DQB1*06:02を超えて）
英語抄録: Narcolepsy type 2 (NT2) is a sleep disorder characterized by excessive daytime sleepiness without cataplexy, a symptom of narcolepsy type 1 (NT1). Almost all NT1 patients carry HLA-DQB1*06:02. Although the positivity of DQB1*06:02 is higher in NT2 (30-50%) than in the general population, it remains considerably lower than in NT1. Previous studies suggest that NT2 comprises heterogeneous subgroups based on DQB1*06:02 status. However, whether NT2 shares a polygenic background with NT1, independent of HLA status, remains unclear. We performed polygenic risk score analyses (PRS) using data from a genome-wide association study of NT1 (5,339 cases and 20,518 controls). Target datasets included 275 NT2 patients, 228 idiopathic hypersomnia (IH) patients, and 1,509 controls. SNPs within the HLA region were excluded to evaluate non-HLA polygenic effects. NT1-derived PRS showed a significant association with NT2 (P = 2.0×10-11). This association remained significant in both DQB1*06:02-positive (P = 2.5×10-7) and -negative NT2 (P = 7.5×10-7) subgroups, indicating that NT2 shares a polygenic background with NT1 independent of HLA status. In contrast, only modest associations were observed between NT1-derived PRS and IH (P = 6.9×10-3). The number of sleep onset REM periods (SOREMPs) in IH patients was associated with higher NT1-derived PRS (P = 3.7×10-4). These findings support genetic continuity between NT1 and NT2 beyond the well-established HLA effect and suggest that non- HLA polygenic factors contribute to susceptibility to NT2, including in DQB1*06:02-negative individuals.

演題名: 生存解析による血清検体中HBV変異の縦断的解析
英語抄録: We previously reported that the HBV basal core promoter mutations A1762T/G1764A markedly increase the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in patients homozygous for HLA-DPB1*05:01 (OR=8.8), whereas HBV mutation alone has been associated with a lower risk (OR=4.1). These findings highlight the importance of monitoring HBV mutation emergence. We aimed to estimate HBV mutation rates using longitudinal serum samples and survival analysis. Serum samples were collected from chronic HBV patients in Japan. HBV mutation status was determined by sequencing serial serum samples. Assuming irreversible mutations and an exponential distribution of waiting time to mutation, mutation rates were estimated using maximum likelihood methods with censored observations. As of January 2025, 881 cases had been collected, and 406 had undergone mutation analysis. HBV mutations were detected in 140 cases, while 73 remained wild type throughout follow-up. Preliminary analysis of 17 patients with wild-type HBV at baseline estimated the mutation rate of A1762T/G1764A to be 8.2×10^-4 per week (approximately 4.2% per year). The exponential model was consistent with Kaplan-Meier estimates, and simulations suggested that >100 cases would provide stable estimates. No reversion from mutant to wild type or emergence of new mutations during nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy was observed. These findings demonstrate that survival analysis of longitudinal serum samples enables estimation of HBV mutation rates and may contribute to prediction of HBV-related hepatocarcinogenesis.

演題名: 日本人集団におけるトリプターゼ遺伝型と食物アレルギーの関連解析
英語抄録: Hereditary α-tryptasemia is an autosomal dominant trait defined by an increase in the copy number of the TPSAB1 gene coding for α or β tryptase. Several studies have demonstrated that an increase in the copy number of α tryptase-coding sequences within the TPSAB1 gene significantly elevates basal serum tryptase levels and raises the prevalence of severe anaphylaxis. Despite these findings in white populations, the relationship between TPSAB1 region CNVs and the anaphylaxis and food allergies in other racial groups, including Asians, remains under-investigated. In this study, we analyzed the TPSAB1 locus in Japanese pediatric samples and examined its association with food allergy and anaphylaxis. The considerable sequence homology between TPSAB1 and TPSB2, which exceeds 97%, makes it difficult to use conventional single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) array-based genotyping techniques. Thus, we used a stepwise genotyping strategy combining long-range PCR, deletion-specific PCR, direct sequencing, quantitative PCR, and droplet digital PCR in a subset of samples to characterize structural variation within the region. The results showed that in Japanese population, increased α-tryptase allele count was rare, whereas the TPSAB1 deletion allele was frequently observed. Furthermore, α-tryptase, β-tryptase, and deletion allele distributions were not associated with food allergy or anaphylaxis. Our findings highlight the importance of population-specific assessment of structurally complex immune-related loci.

演題名: 多祖先GWASが多発性硬化症遺伝学の空間・細胞特性を解明
英語抄録: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the central nervous system characterized by demyelination disseminated in space and time. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in European populations have identified over 200 MS susceptibility loci, but no GWAS has been conducted in East Asian populations. Moreover, recent advancements in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics technologies hold considerable promise for interpreting GWAS findings in MS, which is characterized by spatial heterogeneity, but have not been fully leveraged for this purpose. Here, we performed the first Japanese MS GWAS using 688 cases and 205,199 controls and identified an East Asian-specific risk variant in 11q24. Furthermore, through cross-population GWAS meta-analyses using a total of 29,374 cases and 1,843,563 controls from four ancestral populations, we identified 22 novel loci. To detect cell types associated with MS susceptibility, we integrated our MS GWAS and sc/snRNA-seq datasets. In PBMC scRNA-seq data, MS genetic risk was enriched in CD4+ T cells. In snRNA-seq data from MS subcortical lesions, T cells, myeloid cells, endothelial cells, and B cells showed significant enrichment. Furthermore, we integrated our MS GWAS with spatial transcriptomics of MS subcortical lesions. MS genetic risk was enriched in the "vascular infiltrating" and "lesion rim" regions, specifically in active lesions. Our study underscores the value of investigating spatio-cellular features of disease genetics across diverse populations and omics modalities.

演題名: Cys406のS-ニトロシル化がSBMAにおける異常なアンドロゲン受容体凝集と転写機能障害を引き起こす
英語抄録: Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA) is an adult-onset, X-linked neuromuscular disorder caused by CAG repeat expansion in the androgen receptor (AR). While S-nitrosylation (SNO), a redox-dependent post-translational modification of cysteine thiols, is implicated in aging, cancer, and neurodegeneration, its role in SBMA remains unknown. Here, we identify SNO as a key regulator of AR function by modulating liquid liquid phase separation (LLPS). We focused on Cys406 in the activation function-1, a low-complexity intrinsically disordered region critical for LLPS, and generated a cysteine-to-serine substitution (C406S) in both wild-type AR and polyglutamine-expanded AR (polyQ-AR), abolishing SNO at this site. Confocal imaging revealed that C406S markedly enlarged nuclear AR condensates. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching demonstrated reduced molecular dynamics in C406S mutants, indicating a shift toward more static condensates, with greater effects in polyQ-AR. Functionally, C406S impaired androgen-dependent transcriptional activity, resulting in decreased expression of the AR target genes TMPRSS2 and ERG and reduced MED1 recruitment to AR condensates. Our findings demonstrate that SNO at Cys406 regulates the material properties of AR condensates and transcriptional output, revealing a redox-dependent mechanism linking LLPS dysregulation to SBMA pathogenesis, and suggest that nitrosative stress may contribute to the transcriptional dysfunction observed in this disease.

演題名: 多系統萎縮症におけるBIN1のAGGリピート伸長と凝集
英語抄録: [Introduction] Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by autonomic failure, cerebellar ataxia, and parkinsonism. Although several MSA-associated genetic factors have been reported, the molecular pathogenesis of MSA remains incompletely understood. [Methods] Whole-genome sequencing was performed for a patient with familial MSA. The AGG repeat expansion in BIN1 was screened for 224 patients with clinically diagnosed MSA, 67 patients with pathologically confirmed MSA, and control groups including 574 blood samples and 65 brain samples from neurologically healthy individuals. [Results] Long-read sequencing identified an AGG repeat expansion in the first intron of BIN1 in the proband. Patients with MSA carried a higher frequency of repeat expansions exceeding 80 repeats in the pathological MSA group compared to the brain control group (frequency: 13.4% vs. 0%; odds ratio: infinity; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.1 to infinity; P = 0.003) and in the clinical multiple system atrophy group compared to the blood control group (frequency: 4.5% vs 2.4%; odds ratio: 1.87; 95% CI, 0.8 to 4.5; P = 0.16). Neuropathological analysis revealed BIN1-positive glial cytoplasmic inclusions more frequently in the brains of patients with repeat expansions. In immunoblot analysis, insoluble BIN1 was increased in the brains of multiple system atrophy, irrespective of repeat status. [Discussions] Our findings indicate that the AGG repeat expansion in BIN1 and BIN1 protein aggregation play an important role in the pathogenesis of multiple system atrophy.

演題名: 全ゲノム解析がアミロイドβ蓄積速度に関連する遺伝的リスク因子を明らかにする
英語抄録: Amyloid-β protein (Aβ), the primary component of neuritic plaques in late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD), is considered a key molecular trigger underlying its pathogenesis and progression. However, the Aβ accumulation rate varies substantially among individuals with LOAD, suggesting that individual genetic background may contribute to this variability. In this study, we aimed to identify genetic variants associated with the Aβ accumulation rate using whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data. A total of 139 cognitively normal individuals aged ≥60 (mean age 73.6±5.8 years, 52 females, mean follow-up year 3.1±2.8 years, baseline Centiloid value 15.3±23.1) were included. The Aβ accumulation rate was defined as the annual change in Centiloid values derived from longitudinal Aβ-PET scans. WGS analysis identified common variants and rare variants. Genome-wide association studies for common variants were performed using the Aβ accumulation rate as the dependent variable. Three genome-wide significant and eleven suggestive association signals were identified and further evaluated in an independent validation cohort of 20 participants. As a result, two variants, rs200006811 near AGAP6 and rs142619754 near HAO1, reached genome-wide significance. For rare variants, gene-based association analyses identified eight candidate genes comprising 17 rare variants. Among these, rs61754856 on ADAMTSL3 reached genome-wide significance in replication analysis. These findings may contribute to the development of early-stage prediction models for LOAD and support personalized prevention strategies.

演題名: 日本人特異的な多塩基バリアントとその潜在的制御効果の包括的解析
英語抄録: Large-scale genome studies have advanced rapidly with high-throughput sequencing. While single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) have been extensively characterized across diverse populations, multiple-nucleotide variants (MNVs), defined as clusters of adjacent nucleotide substitutions occurring simultaneously, remain comparatively underexplored, especially in Japanese populations. In this study, we analyzed MNVs using the 60KJPN whole-genome sequencing dataset from the Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization. By comparing MNV allele frequencies with gnomAD, we identified many MNVs observed only in the Japanese dataset (969,700 MNVs; 85.5% of jMorp MNVs). Annotation analysis showed that more than 80% of Japanese MNVs were located in non-coding regions, mainly intergenic and intronic regions, suggesting that their effects may not be captured by coding-focused interpretation. To investigate the potential functional impact of these non-coding MNVs, we applied AlphaGenome, a genome language model, to predict changes in gene expression and epigenomic features. We also compared the predicted effects of MNVs with those of the corresponding SNVs, enabling evaluation of effects that may emerge only when adjacent substitutions are considered jointly. A subset of Japanese-specific MNVs showed predicted regulatory effects that were not fully captured by analysis of the corresponding SNVs alone. These findings highlight the importance of MNV-aware analyses for characterizing population-specific genomic variation and improving the interpretation of disease risk in Japanese populations.

演題名: 日本人集団におけるミトコンドリアDNAコピー数関連バリアントの祖先間移行性
英語抄録: Background: Mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtCN) reflects mitochondrial content and cellular bioenergetic capacity and is influenced by nuclear genetic variation and systemic physiology. However, most genetic determinants of mtCN have been identified in populations of European ancestry, and their transferability to non- European populations remains incompletely understood. Methods: We quantified blood mtCN by quantitative PCR in 857 participants from the Shika population-based cohort in Japan. We applied effect-size equivalence testing to evaluate the transferability of 66 previously reported mtCN-associated variants. We also performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) to identify novel loci and a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) to characterize phenotypic correlates of mtCN. Results: Sixty-two of 66 previously reported mtCN-associated variants showed statistically equivalent effects in our cohort, supporting cross-ancestry transferability of mtCN-associated genetic effects. GWAS identified three loci exceeding the suggestive significance threshold, although none reached genome-wide significance. PheWAS revealed a significant positive association between mtCN and serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels after false discovery rate correction (q = 0.02). Conclusion: These findings support the transferability of previously reported mtCN-associated variants to a Japanese population and suggest that the genetic architecture of mtCN is largely conserved across ancestries. The association between blood mtCN and AST warrants further investigation.

演題名: Trans-ethnicメタ解析がカルバマゼピン誘発SJS/TEN感受性へのHLA-A*31:01の寄与を明らかにする
英語抄録: [Introduction] We demonstrated a strong association between HLA- B*15:11 and carbamazepine (CBZ)-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN) in the Japanese population. In contrast, HLA-A*31:01 is an established risk allele for CBZ-induced drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome/drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DIHS/DRESS), but its contribution to SJS/TEN susceptibility remained unclear. We investigated whether the association between HLA-A*31:01 and SJS/TEN could be replicated by a trans-ethnic meta-analysis of Japanese and Korean cohorts and evaluated the predictive performance of combined HLA biomarkers. [Methods] Meta-analyses were conducted using Japanese and Korean cohorts with CBZ-induced SJS/TEN and DIHS/DRESS. ROC analyses were performed. [Results] The association between HLA-B*15:11 and SJS/TEN was replicated in Japanese and Korean populations. HLA-A*31:01 showed a strong association with DIHS/DRESS and a moderate but statistically significant association with SJS/TEN in the meta-analysis (OR = 3.18, p = 1.1 × 10 -4 ). In the Japanese SJS/TEN cohort, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) increased from 0.698 to 0.749 after adding HLA- A*31:01 to HLA-B*15:11 alone. Similarly, in the Korean SJS/TEN cohort, the AUC improved from 0.681 to 0.793 after adding HLA- A*31:01. [Discussion] These findings suggest that HLA-A*31:01 contributes not only to DIHS/DRESS but also to SJS/TEN susceptibility. Combining HLA-A*31:01 with HLA-B*15:11 substantially improves the prediction of CBZ-induced SJS/TEN in East Asian populations.

演題名: 精神疾患ドナーの死後脳における複雑ゲノム構造多型の検出と解析
英語抄録: Complex structural variations (cxSVs) are often overlooked in genome analyses due to detection challenges. We developed ARC-SV, a probabilistic and machine learning-based method that enables accurate detection and reconstruction of cxSVs from standard datasets. Applying across 4,262 genomes representing all continental populations, we identified cxSVs as a significant source of natural human genetic variation. Rare cxSVs have a propensity to occur in neural genes and loci that underwent rapid human-specific evolution, including those regulating corticogenesis. By performing single-nuclei multiomics in postmortem brains, we discovered cxSVs associated with differential gene expression and chromatin accessibility across various brain regions and cell types. Additionally, cxSVs detected in brains of psychiatric cases are enriched for linkage with psychiatric GWAS risk alleles detected in the same brains. Furthermore, our analysis revealed significantly decreased brain region- and cell type-specific expression of cxSV-genes specifically for psychiatric cases, implicating cxSVs in the molecular etiology of major neuropsychiatric disorders.

演題名: オプティカルゲノムマッピングが発達遅滞3例の複雑な染色体再構成を解明
英語抄録: Conventional cytogenetic analyses may not fully resolve complex chromosomal rearrangements (CCRs). We applied optical genome mapping (OGM) to three patients with developmental delay and suspected CCRs. Case 1 was a 4-year-old boy with macrocephaly, developmental delay, and autistic features. G-banding, FISH, and chromosomal microarray (CMA) identified five structural variants (SVs) involving chromosomes 2, 8, and 14 and a 4.2-Mb deletion at 2q13-q14.1, whereas OGM detected at least 12 SVs, including a breakpoint disrupting CHD8 at 14q11.2. Case 2 was a 6-year-old boy with seizures, developmental delay, and cleft lip and palate. CMA and spectral karyotyping suggested a CCR involving chromosomes 2, 10, 12, and 14, and OGM identified at least 11 translocation breakpoints, clarifying the rearrangement architecture. Case 3 was a 6-year-old boy with developmental delay and infantile epileptic spasms syndrome. G-banding showed 46,XY,t(2;11)(p21;p15.1),t(8;21)(p11.2;q11.2), but OGM identified chromosome 3, rather than chromosome 11, as a rearranged chromosome, revealing a CCR involving chromosomes 2, 3, 8, and 21, four translocation breakpoints, and a 1.13-Mb deletion at 21q21.1. Across all three cases, OGM revealed substantially greater structural complexity than conventional methods. OGM corrected a chromosome misidentification in Case 3 and identified gene-level disruption of CHD8 in Case 1, providing a plausible molecular basis for the phenotype. These findings support OGM for comprehensive characterization of CCRs in patients with developmental delay.
